Managed lane.fact: A managed lane is a type of highway lane that is operated with a management scheme, such as lane use restrictions or variable tolling, to optimize traffic flow, vehicle throughput, or both. Maxim gun.fact: Switzerland Ukraine – Maxim M1910 used during the Russo-Ukrainian War.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Key facts: Maximian (Latin: Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus; c. He shared the latter title with his co-empe
Maximian.answer: Maximian (Latin: Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus; c. He shared the latter title with his co-emperor and superior, Diocletian, whose political brai
Maximian.fact: Maximian (Latin: Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus; c. He shared the latter title with his co-emperor and superior, Diocletian, whose political brain complemented Maximian's military brawn.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: July 310), nicknamed _____, was Roman emperor from 286 to 305
Maximian.fact: July 310), nicknamed Herculius, was Roman emperor from 286 to 305.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He was _____ from 285 to 286, then Augustus from 286 to 305
Maximian.fact: He was Caesar from 285 to 286, then Augustus from 286 to 305.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In late 285, he suppressed rebels in Gaul known as the _____
Maximian.fact: In late 285, he suppressed rebels in Gaul called the Bagaudae.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: From 285 to 288, he fought against _____ tribes along the Rhine frontier
Maximian.fact: From 285 to 288, he fought against Germanic tribes along the Rhine frontier.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Together with _____, he launched a scorched earth campaign deep into Alamannic territory in 288, refortifying the frontier
Maximian.fact: Together with Diocletian, he launched a scorched earth campaign deep into Alamannic territory in 288, refortifying the frontier.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The man he appointed to police the _____ shores, Carausius, rebelled in 286, causing the secession of Britain and northwestern Gaul
Maximian.fact: The man he appointed to police the Channel shores, Carausius, rebelled in 286, causing the secession of Britain and northwestern Gaul.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: When these campaigns concluded in 298, he departed for _____, where he lived in comfort until 305
Maximian.fact: When these campaigns concluded in 298, he departed for Italy, where he lived in comfort until 305. At Diocletian's behest, Maximian abdicated on 1 May 305, gave the Augustan office to Constantius, and retired to southern Italy.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Few supported him, and he was captured by _____ in Marseille
Maximian.fact: In April 307, he attempted to depose his son, but failed and fled to the court of Constantius' successor, Constantine (Maximian's step-grandson and son-in-law), in Trier. In early 310, Maximian attempted to seize Constantine's title while the emperor was on campaign on the Rhine.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Beyond that, the ancient sources contain vague allusions to _____ as his homeland, to his Pannonian virtues, and to his harsh upbringing along the war-torn Danube frontier
Maximian.fact: Beyond that, the ancient sources contain vague allusions to Illyricum as his homeland, to his Pannonian virtues, and to his harsh upbringing along the war-torn Danube frontier.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He probably participated in the _____ campaign of Carus in 283 and attended Diocletian's election as emperor on 20 November 284 at Nicomedia
Maximian.fact: He probably participated in the Mesopotamian campaign of Carus in 283 and attended Diocletian's election as emperor on 20 November 284 at Nicomedia.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: His ambitions were purely military; he left politics to _____
Maximian.fact: His ambitions were purely military; he left politics to Diocletian. The Christian rhetor Lactantius suggested that Maximian shared Diocletian's basic attitudes but was less puritanical in his tastes, and took advantage of the sensual opportunities his position as emperor offered.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Barnes concludes that _____ was born no later than c
Maximian.fact: Maximiana Theodora, the wife of Constantius, is often called Maximian's stepdaughter by ancient sources, leading to claims by Otto Seeck and Ernest Stein that she was born from an earlier marriage between Eutropia and Afranius Hannibalianus. Barnes concludes that Theodora was born no later than c.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: This is in line with _____
Maximian.fact: This is in line with John Vanderspoel.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: With conflict in every province of the _____, from Gaul to Syria, from Egypt to the lower Danube, Diocletian needed a lieutenant to manage his heavy workload
Maximian.fact: With conflict in every province of the Empire, from Gaul to Syria, from Egypt to the lower Danube, Diocletian needed a lieutenant to manage his heavy workload.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Even brief _____ like Volusianus and Numerian, who only held the title for a few months, had coins minted in their names
Maximian.fact: Even brief Caesars like Volusianus and Numerian, who only held the title for a few months, had coins minted in their names.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The panegyric of _____, after comparing his actions to Scipio Africanus' victories over Hannibal during the Second Punic War, suggested that Maximian had never heard of them
Maximian.fact: The panegyric of 289, after comparing his actions to Scipio Africanus' victories over Hannibal during the Second Punic War, suggested that Maximian had never heard of them.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Diocletian was vulnerable in that he had no sons, just a daughter, _____, who could never succeed him
Maximian.fact: Diocletian was vulnerable in that he had no sons, just a daughter, Valeria, who could never succeed him.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Some agree, but the historian _____ has stated that arguments for the adoption are based on misreadings of the papyrological evidence
Maximian.fact: Some agree, but the historian Frank Kolb has stated that arguments for the adoption are based on misreadings of the papyrological evidence.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Finally, _____ knew that single rule was dangerous and that precedent existed for dual rulership
Maximian.fact: The historian William Seston has argued that Diocletian, like heirless emperors before him, adopted Maximian as his filius Augusti ("Augustan son") upon his appointment to the office. Maximian did take Diocletian's nomen (family name) Valerius, however.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Despite their military prowess, both sole-emperors _____ and Probus had been easily removed from power
Maximian.fact: Despite their military prowess, both sole-emperors Aurelian and Probus had been easily removed from power.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In contrast, just a few years earlier, the emperor _____ and his sons had ruled jointly, albeit not for long
Maximian.fact: In contrast, just a few years earlier, the emperor Carus and his sons had ruled jointly, albeit not for long.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Even the first emperor, _____ (r
Maximian.fact: Even the first emperor, Augustus (r. Around 287, after Maximian's appointment as Augustus, the two rulers' relationship was re-defined in religious terms, with Diocletian assuming the title Iovius and Maximian Herculius.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: 27 BC–AD 14), had shared power with his colleagues and more formal offices of co-emperor had existed from _____ (r
Maximian.fact: 27 BC–AD 14), had shared power with his colleagues and more formal offices of co-emperor had existed from Marcus Aurelius (r.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Yet despite the symbolism, the emperors were not "gods" in the _____ cult (although they may have been hailed as such in Imperial panegyrics)
Maximian.fact: Yet despite the symbolism, the emperors were not "gods" in the Imperial cult (although they may have been hailed as such in Imperial panegyrics).

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The fourth-century historian _____ described them as rural people under the leadership of Amandus and Aelianus, while Aurelius Victor called them bandits
Maximian.fact: The fourth-century historian Eutropius described them as rural people under the leadership of Amandus and Aelianus, while Aurelius Victor called them bandits.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Although poorly equipped, led and trained – and therefore a poor match for Roman legions – _____ certainly considered the Bagaudae sufficient threat to merit an emperor to counter them
Maximian.fact: Once the rituals were over, Maximian assumed control of the government of the West and was dispatched to Gaul to fight the rebels called Bagaudae while Diocletian returned to the East. Although poorly equipped, led and trained – and therefore a poor match for Roman legions – Diocletian certainly considered the Bagaudae sufficient threat to merit an emperor to counter them.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: As the campaign was against the _____'s own citizens, and therefore distasteful, it went unrecorded in titles and official triumphs
Maximian.fact: As the campaign was against the Empire's own citizens, and therefore distasteful, it went unrecorded in titles and official triumphs.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In late 285, two barbarian armies – one of _____ and Alamanni, the other of Chaibones and Heruli – forded the Rhine and entered Gaul
Maximian.fact: In late 285, two barbarian armies – one of Burgundians and Alamanni, the other of Chaibones and Heruli – forded the Rhine and entered Gaul.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He then established a Rhine headquarters in preparation for future campaigns, either at _____ (Mainz, Germany), or at Augusta Treverorum (Trier, Germany),
Maximian.fact: He then set up a Rhine headquarters in preparation for future campaigns, either at Moguntiacum (Mainz, Germany), or at Augusta Treverorum (Trier, Germany),.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The emperors Probus and _____ had begun to fortify the Saxon Shore, but much remained to be done
Maximian.fact: The emperors Probus and Carinus had begun to fortify the Saxon Shore, but much remained to be done.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: For example, there is no archaeological evidence of naval bases at Dover and _____ during 270–285
Maximian.fact: For example, there is no archaeological evidence of naval bases at Dover and Boulogne during 270–285.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Carausius quickly eliminated the few remaining loyalists in his army and declared himself _____
Maximian.fact: Carausius quickly eliminated the few remaining loyalists in his army and declared himself Augustus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He had no fleet – he had given it to _____ – and was busy quelling the Heruli and the Franks
Maximian.fact: Carausius' support among the British was strong, and at least two British legions (II Augusta and XX Valeria Victrix) defected to him, as did some or all of a legion near Boulogne (probably XXX Ulpia Victrix). Carausius quickly eliminated the few remaining loyalists in his army and declared himself Augustus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Meanwhile, _____ strengthened his position by enlarging his fleet, enlisting Frankish mercenaries, and paying his troops well
Maximian.fact: Carausius quickly eliminated the few remaining loyalists in his army and declared himself Augustus. He had no fleet – he had given it to Carausius – and was busy quelling the Heruli and the Franks.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: By late 286, _____, much of northwestern Gaul, and the entire Channel coast, was under his control
Maximian.fact: By late 286, Britain, much of northwestern Gaul, and the entire Channel coast, was under his control.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: This suggestion has not won much support, and the historian _____ has recently refuted it
Maximian.fact: This suggestion has not won much support, and the historian William Leadbetter has recently refuted it.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In theory, the _____ was not divided by the dual imperium
Maximian.fact: In theory, the Roman Empire was not divided by the dual imperium.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Imperial propaganda from 287 on insists on a singular and indivisible _____, a patrimonium indivisum
Maximian.fact: Imperial propaganda from 287 on insists on a singular and indivisible Rome, a patrimonium indivisum.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: These tribes were probably greater threats to _____ peace anyway and included many supporters of Carausius
Maximian.fact: These tribes were probably greater threats to Gallic peace anyway and included many supporters of Carausius.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Doffing his toga and donning his armor, he marched against the barbarians and, although they were not entirely dispersed, he celebrated a victory in _____ later that year
Maximian.fact: Doffing his toga and donning his armor, he marched against the barbarians and, although they were not entirely dispersed, he celebrated a victory in Gaul later that year.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He fought in person, riding along the battle line until the _____ forces broke
Maximian.fact: He fought in person, riding along the battle line until the Germanic forces broke. He moved deep into Germanic territory, bringing destruction to his enemies' homelands.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He moved deep into _____ territory, bringing destruction to his enemies' homelands
Maximian.fact: He fought in person, riding along the battle line until the Germanic forces broke. He moved deep into Germanic territory, bringing destruction to his enemies' homelands.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: By the end of 287, he had the advantage and the _____ lands were free of Germanic tribesmen
Maximian.fact: By the end of 287, he had the advantage and the Rhenish lands were free of Germanic tribesmen.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: They probably agreed on a joint campaign against the _____ and a naval expedition against Carausius
Maximian.fact: They probably agreed on a joint campaign against the Alamanni and a naval expedition against Carausius. Later in the year, Maximian led a surprise invasion of the Agri Decumates – a region between the upper Rhine and upper Danube deep within Alamanni territory – while Diocletian invaded Germany via Raetia.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Both emperors burned crops and food supplies as they went, destroying the _____' means of sustenance
Maximian.fact: Both emperors burned crops and food supplies as they went, destroying the Germans' means of sustenance.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: These Franks controlled the Rhine estuaries, thwarting sea-attacks against _____
Maximian.fact: These Franks controlled the Rhine estuaries, thwarting sea-attacks against Carausius.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Constantius moved north through their territory, wreaking havoc, and reaching the _____
Maximian.fact: Constantius moved north through their territory, wreaking havoc, and reaching the North Sea.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: These tribes were allowed to settle on the condition that they acknowledged _____ dominance
Maximian.fact: Gennobaudes became Maximian's vassal and, with lesser Frankish chiefs in turn swearing loyalty to Gennobaudes, Roman regional dominance was assured. Maximian allowed a settlement of Frisii, Salian Franks, Chamavi and other tribes along a strip of Roman territory, either between the Rhine and Waal rivers from Noviomagus (Nijmegen, Netherlands) to Traiectum, (Utrecht, Netherlands) or near Trier.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Diocletian returned in haste to the West, reaching Emesa by 10 May 290, and _____ on the Danube by 1 July 290
Maximian.fact: Diocletian returned in haste to the West, reaching Emesa by 10 May 290, and Sirmium on the Danube by 1 July 290.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Potter, among others, has surmised that the ceremonies were arranged to demonstrate _____'s continuing support for his faltering colleague
Maximian.fact: Diocletian returned in haste to the West, reaching Emesa by 10 May 290, and Sirmium on the Danube by 1 July 290. Diocletian met Maximian in Milan either in late December 290 or January 291.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The rulers discussed matters of politics and war in secret, and they may have considered the idea of expanding the imperial college to include four rulers (the _____)
Maximian.fact: The rulers discussed matters of politics and war in secret, and they may have considered the idea of expanding the imperial college to include four rulers (the Tetrarchy).

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Meanwhile, a deputation from the _____ met with the rulers and renewed its infrequent contact with the imperial office
Maximian.fact: Meanwhile, a deputation from the Roman Senate met with the rulers and renewed its infrequent contact with the imperial office.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: For his part, _____ was content with his territories beyond the Continental coast of Gaul
Maximian.fact: Following Maximian's failure to invade in 289, an uneasy truce with Carausius began. Maximian tolerated Carausius' rule in Britain and on the continent but refused to grant the secessionist state formal legitimacy.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Faced with _____' secession and further challenges on the Egyptian, Syrian, and Danubian borders, he realized that two emperors were insufficient to manage the Empire
Maximian.fact: Maximian tolerated Carausius' rule in Britain and on the continent but refused to grant the secessionist state formal legitimacy. For his part, Carausius was content with his territories beyond the Continental coast of Gaul.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: On either the same day or a month later, _____ did the same for Galerius, thus establishing the "Tetrarchy", or "rule of four"
Maximian.fact: Diocletian, however, would not tolerate this affront to his rule. On either the same day or a month later, Diocletian did the same for Galerius, thus establishing the "Tetrarchy", or "rule of four".

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In the same year, _____ was assassinated and replaced by his treasurer, Allectus
Maximian.fact: Constantius was made to understand that he must succeed where Maximian had failed and defeat Carausius. In the same year, Carausius was assassinated and replaced by his treasurer, Allectus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Constantius marched up the coast to the Rhine and _____ estuaries where he was victorious over Carausius' Frankish allies, taking the title Germanicus maximus
Maximian.fact: Constantius marched up the coast to the Rhine and Scheldt estuaries where he was victorious over Carausius' Frankish allies, taking the title Germanicus maximus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: His sights now set on _____, Constantius spent the following years building an invasion fleet
Maximian.fact: His sights now set on Britain, Constantius spent the following years building an invasion fleet. There, he held the Rhenish frontiers against Carausius' Frankish allies while Constantius launched his invasion of Britain.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: There, he held the _____ frontiers against Carausius' Frankish allies while Constantius launched his invasion of Britain
Maximian.fact: There, he held the Rhenish frontiers against Carausius' Frankish allies while Constantius launched his invasion of Britain.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Allectus was killed on the _____ in battle with Constantius' praetorian prefect, Asclepiodotus
Maximian.fact: Allectus was killed on the North Downs in battle with Constantius' praetorian prefect, Asclepiodotus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Constantius himself had landed near Dubris (Dover) and marched on _____ (London), whose citizens greeted him as a liberator
Maximian.fact: Constantius himself had landed near Dubris (Dover) and marched on Londinium (London), whose citizens greeted him as a liberator.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: As Roman authority weakened during the third century, nomadic _____ tribes harassed settlements in the region with increasingly severe consequences
Maximian.fact: As Roman authority weakened during the third century, nomadic Berber tribes harassed settlements in the region with increasingly severe consequences.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In 289, the governor of _____ (roughly modern Algeria) gained a temporary respite by pitting a small army against the Bavares and Quinquegentiani, but the raiders soon returned
Maximian.fact: In 289, the governor of Mauretania Caesariensis (roughly modern Algeria) gained a temporary respite by pitting a small army against the Bavares and Quinquegentiani, but the raiders soon returned.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He may have defended the region against raiding Moors before crossing the Strait of Gibraltar into _____ (roughly modern Morocco) to protect the area from Frankish pirates
Maximian.fact: He may have defended the region against raiding Moors before crossing the Strait of Gibraltar into Mauretania Tingitana (roughly modern Morocco) to protect the area from Frankish pirates.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Apparently wishing to inflict as much punishment as possible on the tribes, he devastated previously secure land, killed as many as he could, and drove the remainder back into the _____
Maximian.fact: Apparently wishing to inflict as much punishment as possible on the tribes, he devastated previously secure land, killed as many as he could, and drove the remainder back into the Sahara.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: His campaign was concluded by early 298 and, on 10 March, he made a triumphal entry into _____
Maximian.fact: His campaign was concluded by early 298 and, on 10 March, he made a triumphal entry into Carthage.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In contrast, _____ kept up good relations with the senatorial aristocracy and spent his time in active defense of the empire
Maximian.fact: After his Mauretanian campaign in 299, Maximian returned to the north of Italy, living a life of leisure in palaces in Milan and Aquilea, and leaving warfare to his subordinate Constantius. Maximian was more aggressive in his relationship with the Senate than Constantius, and Lactantius contends that he terrorized senators, to the point of falsely charging and subsequently executing several, including the prefect of Rome in 301–2.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: According to _____, he also built a palace near his home town of Sirmium
Maximian.fact: According to Aurelius Victor, he also built a palace near his home town of Sirmium.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Diocletian retired to the expansive palace he had built in his homeland, _____ near Salona on the Adriatic
Maximian.fact: Diocletian retired to the expansive palace he had built in his homeland, Dalmatia near Salona on the Adriatic.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: This displeased _____, who instead offered Constantine the title of Caesar, which Constantine accepted
Maximian.fact: This displeased Galerius, who instead offered Constantine the title of Caesar, which Constantine accepted.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The title of _____ then went to Severus
Maximian.fact: The title of Augustus then went to Severus. Maxentius was jealous of Constantine's power, and on 28 October 306, he persuaded a cohort of imperial guardsmen to declare him Augustus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Maxentius was jealous of _____'s power, and on 28 October 306, he persuaded a cohort of imperial guardsmen to declare him Augustus
Maximian.fact: This displeased Galerius, who instead offered Constantine the title of Caesar, which Constantine accepted. Maxentius was jealous of Constantine's power, and on 28 October 306, he persuaded a cohort of imperial guardsmen to declare him Augustus.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Galerius refused to recognize _____ and sent Severus with an army to Rome to depose him
Maximian.fact: Maxentius was jealous of Constantine's power, and on 28 October 306, he persuaded a cohort of imperial guardsmen to declare him Augustus. Uncomfortable with sole leadership, Maxentius sent a set of imperial robes to Maximian and saluted him as "Augustus for the second time", offering him theoretic equal rule but less actual power and a lower rank.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In late _____, Galerius led a second force against Maxentius but he again failed to take Rome, and retreated north with his army mostly intact
Maximian.fact: In late 307, Galerius led a second force against Maxentius but he again failed to take Rome, and retreated north with his army mostly intact. The deal was sealed with a double ceremony in Trier in late 307, at which Constantine married Fausta and was declared Augustus by Maximian.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He spoke of Rome's sickly government, disparaged _____ for having weakened it, and ripped the imperial toga from Maxentius' shoulders
Maximian.fact: In return, Constantine would reaffirm the old family alliance between Maximian and Constantius, and support Maxentius' cause in Italy but would remain neutral in the war with Galerius. He spoke of Rome's sickly government, disparaged Maxentius for having weakened it, and ripped the imperial toga from Maxentius' shoulders.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Licinius, a loyal military companion to _____, was appointed Augustus of the West
Maximian.fact: On 11 November 308, to resolve the political instability, Galerius called Diocletian (out of retirement) and Maximian to a general council meeting at the military city of Carnuntum on the upper Danube. Licinius, a loyal military companion to Galerius, was appointed Augustus of the West.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Constantine and _____ refused to be placated with the titles of Sons of the Augusti, and they were both reluctantly recognized as emperors, with the result that there were now four Augusti
Maximian.fact: There, Maximian was forced to abdicate again and Constantine was again demoted to Caesar, with Maximinus the Caesar in the east. Constantine and Maximinus refused to be placated with the titles of Sons of the Augusti, and they were both reluctantly recognized as emperors, with the result that there were now four Augusti.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: The town was better able to withstand a long siege than Arles, but it made little difference as loyal citizens opened the rear gates to _____
Maximian.fact: In Arles, Maximian announced that Constantine was dead and took up the imperial purple. Although Maximian offered bribes to all who would support him, most of Constantine's army remained loyal, and Maximian was compelled to leave the city.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Fausta learned of the plot and warned _____, who put a eunuch in his own place in bed
Maximian.fact: Constantine initially presented the suicide as an unfortunate family tragedy. According to this, after Constantine had pardoned him, Maximian planned to murder Constantine in his sleep.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Constantine defeated _____ at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 312
Maximian.fact: Constantine defeated Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 312. Maxentius died, and Italy came under Constantine's rule.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: His apotheosis under _____ was declared null and void, and he was re-consecrated as a god, probably in 317
Maximian.fact: Constantine defeated Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 312. Maxentius died, and Italy came under Constantine's rule.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: Maxentius died, and Italy came under _____'s rule
Maximian.fact: In addition to the propaganda, Constantine instituted a damnatio memoriae on Maximian, destroying all inscriptions referring to him and eliminating any public work bearing his image. Constantine defeated Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 312.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: He began appearing on _____'s coinage as divus, or divine, by 318, together with the deified Constantius and Claudius Gothicus The three were hailed as Constantine's forebears
Maximian.fact: Maxentius died, and Italy came under Constantine's rule. He began appearing on Constantine's coinage as divus, or divine, by 318, together with the deified Constantius and Claudius Gothicus The three were hailed as Constantine's forebears.

Maximian.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximian.question: In late 307, _____ led a second force against Maxentius but he again failed to take Rome, and retreated north with his army mostly intact
Maximian.fact: In late 307, Galerius led a second force against Maxentius but he again failed to take Rome, and retreated north with his army mostly intact. In return, Constantine would reaffirm the old family alliance between Maximian and Constantius, and support Maxentius' cause in Italy but would remain neutral in the war with Galerius.

Maximilian Grabner.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximilian Grabner.question: Maximilian Grabner (2 October _____ – 24 January 1948) was an Austrian Gestapo chief in Auschwitz
Maximilian Grabner.fact: Maximilian Grabner (2 October 1905 – 24 January 1948) was an Austrian Gestapo chief in Auschwitz.

Maximilian Grabner.subject: Applied Sciences
Maximilian Grabner.question: At Auschwitz he was in command of the torture chamber _____ 11, where he gained a reputation of brutality
Maximilian Grabner.fact: At Auschwitz he was in command of the torture chamber Block 11, where he gained a reputation of brutality.

Maximilian Grabner.subject: Applied Sciences
